findings.title: Dereference of a nullable lookup result
findings.claim: Dereference of a nullable lookup result: available=false reaches p->value with p equal to nullptr.
findings.reasoning_summary: available=false is passed unchanged to review_lookup, whose false branch returns nullptr. The same p is dereferenced on the next statement with no intervening guard or write.
findings.suggestion: Check p immediately after lookup or return a non-null result with a documented invariant.

findings.title: Guard checks a different pointer
findings.claim: Guard checks a different pointer: available=false reaches p->value with p equal to nullptr.
findings.reasoning_summary: available=false makes p null. q points to the distinct local object other, so if (!q) does not return and does not validate p; p->value remains reachable.
findings.suggestion: Check p before accessing its value; checking q does not constrain p.

findings.title: Reassignment invalidates the earlier null check
findings.claim: Reassignment invalidates the earlier null check: available=true reaches a null dereference after the second lookup.
findings.reasoning_summary: With available=true the first lookup passes the guard. The subsequent review_lookup(false) unconditionally returns nullptr and overwrites p before p->value.
findings.suggestion: Validate the new lookup result after reassignment, or avoid overwriting the checked pointer.
